title: RV-04 review: Bounded local daily-story consumer
rationale: The local consumer remains separate from ingestion and actuation, but this diff changes an already-defined story column by editing its historical migration instead of adding forward migration DDL. It also injects a private environment object into a model prompt whose generated story is public without a semantic non-leak boundary, and it lacks the representative local-model acceptance required for the changed prompt/runtime/output budget.
scope_architecture: The worker is an optional bounded LLM consumer and no changed path reaches ingestion, control, Guardrails, Executor, or hardware. Its persistent run shape, public story response, prompt/context limits, and model runtime behavior nevertheless form schema and public-output contracts.

findings.finding: The diff changes the story column length by editing revision 0007, but the new forward revision only adds environment_context_jsonb and does not alter the existing column.
findings.evidence: An installation that already applied revision 0007 will not rerun its edited create-table statement. Revision 0008 adds only the context column, while the application now accepts stories through 32768 characters.
findings.impact: Upgraded databases can retain the prior shorter column and fail when the newly accepted long-form story is persisted, breaking the normal daily-story execution path.
findings.required_change: Add a new forward Alembic revision that alters the existing story column and test upgrade from a database already at revision 0007; do not rely on editing an applied migration.
findings.suggested_test: Run an upgrade from the pre-existing 0007 schema, persist a valid story longer than the old bound, and verify the stored value and API serialization.

findings.finding: The worker serializes the whole private environment context into the model prompt but has no semantic validation that prevents that raw context from being echoed into the publishable story.
findings.evidence: The README describes the environment object as private and excluded from the public API, while the changed template injects it into model-visible text. _parse_story checks JSON shape, length, and a suffix only; the added tests do not inject a private marker and assert it cannot appear in the public story.
findings.impact: A model can reproduce sensitive operator-maintained facts or prompt content in the story field even though the stored context column itself is omitted from the API.
findings.required_change: Pass only a deliberately public/sanitized projection to the model that creates public stories, or add a robust output privacy boundary and regression tests proving injected private markers cannot be returned.
findings.suggested_test: Test a generated response containing a unique private-context marker and verify the public story serialization rejects or redacts it.

findings.finding: The supplied report marks manual evidence not applicable even though the diff changes the prompt, model request shape, fallback behavior, context/output budgets, and publishable output contract.
findings.evidence: The test matrix requires representative local-model acceptance when model/runtime behavior changes. The fixture reports only historical automated model-boundary/application tests and explicitly supplies no manual acceptance; fake-client tests do not establish that the configured model can complete the full bounded prompt safely.
findings.evidence_excerpt: NOT APPLICABLE: no physical or production action is in scope
findings.impact: A model/runtime-specific grammar, context, timeout, reasoning, or privacy failure can reach the optional worker without the required representative evidence.
findings.required_change: Record a representative local-model acceptance covering the full prompt/context, malformed and unavailable responses, semantic/privacy rejection, timeout behavior, and the configured output budget; classify the schema/public-output migration checks in the brief.
findings.suggested_test: Run the documented local daily-story acceptance with the configured model and a synthetic privacy marker, then verify bounded completion and public-output exclusion.

contract_consumer_review: Changed consumers include the daily-story database row, migration chain, worker, Ollama client, private stored context, prompt templates, Compose environment, and public story API. Tests cover fake-client parsing and omission of the private database field, but not the upgraded database schema or an end-to-end model-output privacy boundary.

evidence_matrix.check: Approved fixture brief and pinned diff identity
Historical model-boundary and application tests supplied in implementation report
Representative local-model acceptance and privacy check

operations_safety_security_privacy: No actuation path is introduced. The changed model consumer has a public-output privacy boundary and schema-migration risk that cannot be closed by fake-client tests alone.
documentation_assessment: The documentation states that environment context is private and excluded from the API, but it does not reconcile that claim with supplying the full object to a model that produces the public story.
limitations: Review was restricted to the fixture brief/report, stable rules, and pinned diff; no local model, production data, private context, or external Ollama service was run.
No assumptions were made about the contents of any operator-maintained runtime environment context.
